$P(t)=500e^{kt}$ where $k=\dfrac{\ln\frac{83}{25}}{120}$

$$\begin{aligned}P'(t)&=500ke^{kt}\\ P'(120)&=500ke^{k\times 120}\\ &=16.6\ldots\end{aligned}$$

$\therefore$ Increasing at approximately 17 bacteria/min at $t=120$.

$$\begin{aligned}P'(t)&=500ke^{kt}\quad\text{where }k=\dfrac{\ln\frac{83}{25}}{120}\\ P''(t)&=500k^2e^{kt}\end{aligned}$$

$e^{kt}$ is $>0$ for all $t$, so $P'(t)>0$ and $P''(t)>0$ for all $t$.

$\therefore\ P(t)$ and $P'(t)$ are both always increasing

$\therefore\ P(t)$ is increasing at an increasing rate and therefore a control mechanism should be introduced.

Let $\dfrac{dA}{dr}=0$:

$$\begin{aligned}0&=-20\pi+2\pi^2r+4\pi r\\ 20\pi&=2\pi^2r+4\pi r\\ 10&=\pi r+2r\\ 10&=r(\pi+2)\\ r&=\dfrac{10}{\pi+2}\end{aligned}$$

Check nature using $\dfrac{d^2A}{dr^2}$:

$\dfrac{d^2A}{dr^2}=2\pi^2+4\pi$ which is $>0$ for all $r$

At $r=\dfrac{10}{\pi+2}$,

solutions.latex:
$$\begin{aligned}A_{\text{curve}}&=\int_0^4 p^x\,dx\\ &=\left[\dfrac{p^x}{\ln p}\right]_0^4\\ &=\dfrac{p^4}{\ln p}-\dfrac{p^0}{\ln p}\\ &=\dfrac{p^4-1}{\ln p}\end{aligned}$$

From diagram, $A_{\text{rect}}<A_{\text{curve}}$

$$\begin{aligned}\therefore\ \dfrac{p^4-1}{p-1}&<\dfrac{p^4-1}{\ln p}\\ \dfrac{1}{p-1}&<\dfrac{1}{\ln p}\\ \ln p&<p-1\quad\text{as }p>1\end{aligned}$$

Since $f(t)$ is a PDF, $\displaystyle\int_0^6 f(t)\,dt=1$

$$\begin{aligned}1&=k\int_0^6 36t-t^3\,dt\\ 1&=k\left[18t^2-\dfrac{t^4}{4}\right]_0^6\\ 1&=k\left(18(6)^2-\dfrac{6^4}{4}-0\right)\\ 1&=648k-324k\\ 1&=324k\\ k&=\dfrac{1}{324}\text{ as required}\end{aligned}$$

Mode occurs when $f(t)$ reaches max:

$$\begin{aligned}f(t)&=36kt-kt^3\\ &=\dfrac{t}{9}-\dfrac{t^3}{324}\\ f'(t)&=\dfrac{1}{9}-\dfrac{3t^2}{324}\end{aligned}$$

Let $f'(t)=0$:

$$\begin{aligned}0&=\dfrac{1}{9}-\dfrac{3t^2}{324}\\ \dfrac{3t^2}{324}&=\dfrac{1}{9}\\ t^2&=12\\ t&=\sqrt{12}\quad(t>0)\\ t&=2\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}$$

Check nature:

$$\begin{aligned}f''(t)&=-\dfrac{6t}{324}\\ f''(2\sqrt{3})&=-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{27}\end{aligned}$$

$f''(2\sqrt{3})<0$ $\therefore$ max at $t=2\sqrt{3}$

$\therefore$ Mode is $2\sqrt{3}$.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: $t=2\sqrt{3}$; 1: checks nature to show a maximum (must show for 2/2)

notes: Cover: ABBOTSLEIGH, '2024 Higher School Certificate Trial Examination', Mathematics Advanced, total 100 marks (Section I 10 marks Q1-10, Section II 90 marks Q11-16, 15 marks each); matches expected label 2024 Abbotsleigh AT4 (trial = AT4, 2024 HSC cohort). PDF is 112 pages: pages 0-55 the blank booklet, pages 56-111 the same booklet with handwritten teacher solutions (red, some dark blue working) and light-blue mark allocations. Questions transcribed from pages 2-52; solutions from 58-108 (MCQ answers circled with working; source extracted). Marks breakdowns are read from the blue circled marks. Skipped: page 1 outcomes, blank pages, extra writing pages. Blank answer axes in Q13(a) and Q15(b)(ii) and the answer box in Q12(e)(iii) are answer space and were not cropped. Q9 z-table is an image and was cropped as a figure; Q12(b), Q13(c), Q16(a) tables transcribed. Solution sketches cropped from the solution copy with light-blue marking annotations whitened out (Q7 sketch kept as is). Paper slips kept as printed: page 47 footer reads 'Question 15 continues on page 48' (Q16); Q12(e)(i) 'equation relating x in terms of y'; Q15(b)(ii) says x-intercepts for a v-t graph. Source solution slips transcribed as written: Q14(b) takes P(N2)=2/8 (four cards have a second 'a', so by the usual reading P(N2)=1/2 and N1, N2 ARE independent - flagged); Q14(c)(ii) GP sum denominator written 1.005 (should be 0.005); Q16(c)(iii) primitive t^4/324 (should be t^4/1296; values use 1296) and final line written P(X>3|X<1). Q14(d) is 3D trigonometry: marked old_syllabus for part (d). Unrelated parts are grouped under Questions 11-16 as printed (split_questions.py can split them after loading).
